title: Marked coanodyne extensions
statement: Use simplicial sets, horns, Kan complexes and universes from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and marked simplicial sets, their products, and the markings $X^\flat,X^\sharp$ from [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. A map of marked simplicial sets is a cofibration when its underlying map is degreewise injective. The marked coanodyne class is the smallest class containing isomorphisms and the following maps and closed under pushouts, small transfinite compositions, and retracts in the arrow category: (i) $(\Lambda_i^n)^\flat\hookrightarrow(\Delta^n)^\flat$ for $0<i<n$; (ii) $(\Lambda_0^n,T|_{\Lambda_0^n})\hookrightarrow(\Delta^n,T)$ for $n\geq1$, where $T$ consists of the degenerate edges and the initial edge $\{0,1\}$; (iii) the map from $\Delta^2$ with just the degenerate and consecutive edges $\{0,1\},\{1,2\}$ marked to $(\Delta^2)^\sharp$; (iv) $L^\flat\to L^\sharp$ for each small Kan complex $L$. Thus this class is the opposite of the marked anodyne class used for cartesian fibrations; it is not the unmarked inner-anodyne class. Pushouts have the simplicial pushout as underlying simplicial set and the images of the marked edges as marking. For marked simplicial sets $U,W$, write $W^U$ for their marked internal Hom: its underlying $n$-simplices are marked maps $U\times(\Delta^n)^\flat\to W$, and an edge is marked when its corresponding map $U\times(\Delta^1)^\flat\to W$ preserves the additional markings of $U\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp$.
